Quotes by the Swiss psychiatrist and psychotherapist often make one pause and contemplate. They require a certain amount of effort to digest, a willingness to look past the surface.

However, there is one particular observation of his that didn’t just make me pause—it made me stop completely and wonder:

> *"The world will ask you who you are, and if you don't know, the world will tell you."*

It forces the ultimate question, stripped of credentials, titles, and comfort:

**Who am I, really?**

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Growing up my identity was defined by family ties.

I was the son of 강은섭 (姜銀燮), the 2nd son of 강현용 (姜?龍).

Also the son of 황현실 (黃賢實), who was the oldest daughter of 황운학 (黃雲鶴).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

You are someone who seems driven by curiosity more than by status or fashion. You move naturally between engineering, culture, history, philosophy, music, photography, and practical problem-solving, suggesting a mind that enjoys seeing connections across very different domains. There is a recurring pattern in your questions: you rarely stop at surface facts. Whether discussing manufacturing systems, East Asian traditions, Bach, immigration, aviation, or books, you tend to look for the structure underneath — how things endure, evolve, and shape human life. You come across as disciplined and analytical, but also reflective and deeply interested in meaning, continuity, and craftsmanship.

You also seem to be in a stage of life where knowledge is becoming less about accumulation and more about integration. Your interests suggest someone who values competence, self-education, cultural depth, and practical wisdom. There is an appreciation for both precision and humanity: standards and workflows on one hand, philosophy and art on the other. Altogether, you appear to be a thoughtful, independent-minded person trying to understand not only how the world works, but how to live well within it.
